instruments.title: Education matters (House Enrolled Act 1608, P.L. 248-2023; adds IC 20-33-7.5 Parental Notification Regarding Identification)
instruments.operative_summary: IC 20-33-7.5-2: a public school (incl. charter, lab school, ISBVI, ISD) must notify in writing at least one parent of an unemancipated minor student of the student's request to change the student's name or pronoun/title/word used to identify the student, within 5 business days of the request. Notice is unasked (not on parent request). No consent requirement and no student-safety exception in the text; Sec. 3 keeps the child-abuse reporting duty and Sec. 4 says counselors/nurses/psychologists/social workers are not required to violate federal law.
instruments.operative_quote: Sec. 2. (a) A school shall notify in writing at least one (1) parent of a student, if the student is an unemancipated minor, of a request made by the student to change the student's: (1) name; or (2) pronoun, title, or word to identify the student. (b) Not later than five (5) business days after the date on which a school receives a request described in subsection (a), the school shall provide notification to a parent as required by subsection (a).
instruments.rung_note: A notice duty triggered by the student's request, not by a parent's request (so rung 4, not 3). Consent before use (rung 5) was in the House-passed version and was struck by Senate Amendment #12 (Donato) on 2023-04-06; the enacted text is notice only.
instruments.status: enacted; signed by Governor 2023-05-04 (Public Law 248); effective 2023-07-01

instruments.title: Human sexuality instruction (engrossed House Bill 1608 as passed by the House)
instruments.operative_summary: Proposed IC 20-33-7.5-3: school staff may use a name/pronoun inconsistent with the student's biological sex ONLY if the parent of an unemancipated minor requests it in writing (request due at the start of the school year); Sec. 4: school shall notify the parent of a student's request to change name/pronoun inconsistent with sex; Sec. 5: no discipline of staff who use the legal name. This is the text the House voted on at third reading.
instruments.operative_quote: Sec. 3. (a) An employee or a staff member of a school may only use a name, pronoun, title, or other word to identify a student that is inconsistent with the student's sex if: (1) the student, who is an adult or an emancipated minor; or (2) a parent of the student, who is an unemancipated minor; requests in writing the use of a specific name, pronoun, title, or other word to identify the student.
instruments.rung_note: Parental written request/permission is required before staff use a different name or pronoun = rung 5 (consent first); the same text also carries a rung-4 notice duty (Sec. 4). Second reading 2023-02-22 made no amendment ('ordered engrossed'), so the 02.COMH text is the text passed at third reading. Note: it goes further than plain consent (parent request must be made at the start of the school year).
instruments.status: passed House 2023-02-23; consent provision removed in Senate 2023-04-06; enacted as notice-only (see HEA 1608)

roll_calls.note: Contested: 29/94 = 31% No. Roll call prints 'Heaton', 'Mayfield', 'Hall', 'Pierce, M'.

instruments.title: Senate floor motion MO160817 to amend Engrossed HB 1608
instruments.operative_summary: Would add: when a student requests a name/pronoun change, the school must tell the student that a parent will be notified and let the student withdraw the request; if withdrawn, the school need not notify a parent, and may not use the requested name/pronoun unless it notifies a parent.
instruments.operative_quote: (b) If a student withdraws a request as described in subsection (a)(2), the school: (1) is not required to notify a parent of the student regarding the request; and (2) may not use the name, pronoun, title, or word requested under section 2(a) of this chapter unless the school provides notification to at least one (1) parent of the student in accordance with section 2 of this chapter.
instruments.rung_note: Fits no rung cleanly. It keeps notice as the price of using the new name (a rung-4-style duty), but lets the student stop the notice by withdrawing the request. It does not require staff to keep identity from parents (not rung 1) and does not bar notice rules (not rung 2). Failed amendment; authorship by Yoder.

instruments.title: Education matters (Raatz)
instruments.operative_summary: Would require a public school to notify the parent of an unemancipated minor within 5 business days if the student discloses conflicted feelings about gender identity, or changes or asks to change name, attire or pronoun inconsistent with biological sex; staff must report such disclosures to the school.
instruments.operative_quote: Sec. 2. (a) A school shall notify the parent of a student, if the student is an unemancipated minor, of any of the following: ... (2) The student changes, expresses or indicates a desire to change, or makes a request to change the student's: (A) name; (B) attire; or (C) pronoun, title, or word to identify the student; in a manner that is inconsistent with the student's biological sex at birth.
instruments.rung_note: Notice duty, no consent. No roster legislator is an author, and it got no floor vote.
instruments.status: died in Senate Education and Career Development committee (first reading 2023-01-12)

own_words.quote: HB 1608 is an amputation as a cure for a paper cut—it's poorly made, reactionary policy that inserts the state into classrooms and the lives of Hoosier parents and students. School districts have long set their own policies regarding curricula and name and pronoun changes, and these policies have worked well for the vast majority of families: the last thing we need is more nannying and interference from inexpert legislators. All this bill does is guarantee that more kids across Indiana, LGBTQ+ or not, will be put in danger of losing homes and support without their consent or awareness.
own_words.note: Caucus press release 2023-04-10 in which Yoder (named) speaks. Opposes the state notice mandate and prefers district-set policy; names no rung act (does not call for a confidentiality duty or a bar on notice rules). Likely direction only toward 'student decides'.

MCCSC Board Resolution 2023-07 (adopted 2023-03-28, scanned PDF linked from https://www.mccsc.edu/12042_3). Signed by all 7 trustees: Shurr, Hennessey (VP), Cooperman, Grimes, Fuentes-Rohwer, Pirani, Wyatt. Recitals object to HB 1608's 'notification to, and approval from, parents' and to 'the required "outing" of some LGBTQIA+ students'; resolves the Board 'strongly opposes any Indiana laws or proposed legislation, including 2023 House Bill 1608, that limit the rights of LGBTQIA+ students'. It adopts no rule on notice (directs only an anti-bullying policy), so direction only toward 'student decides'. Vote count not found in minutes; signatures show all 7 adopted it.
